- Description: Sophia Telegram reliability sweep — role-loop, mention-gating, deploy-order, emoji-reaction deadlock
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/340
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/341

  Details:
  Gary reported Sophia's Telegram autopilot felt broken tonight ("a lot of the stuff with her is mid task right now and has been for hours... I wonder if it has to do with the emoji implementation"). Traced and fixed 7 real bugs across the night, most unrelated to the emoji feature itself but surfaced while diagnosing it:
  
  1. PR #340 — list_prs() threw IndexError on repos with few PRs (PyGithub PaginatedList slice bug), silently blocking a queued sunmint_beta PR request.
  2. PR #341 — /chat/observe (group mention-gating) silently broke the new-topic default-role bootstrap: a topic could get permanently stuck on "I couldn't parse a role" because unmentioned chatter polluted its history before a role was ever set.
  3. PR #342 — the bot's own @mention was never stripped from dispatched text, so even a correctly-mentioned "7" reply to the role prompt failed to parse.
  4. PR #343 — mention-gating silently swallowed Gary's own name-based addressing ("@sophia", not the literal @bot_username) and any mid-turn follow-up sent while a turn was actively running, with zero acknowledgment either way.
  5. PR #344 — dropped the "RESUME HERE" regex/resume_awaiting gate per Gary's explicit ask: any positive emoji reaction on any of her messages now means "continue," not just specially-flagged ones.
  6. PR #345 — found and fixed why deploys were silently leaving 3 of 4 autopilot systemd services (telegram/watchdog/vault) stuck on old code: the restart command listed the self-referencing service FIRST, killing the systemctl client mid-command before it reached the rest of the list.
  7. PR #346 — found and fixed a genuine self-deadlock: the emoji-reaction resume path double-acquired the same non-reentrant per-thread lock, so every successful thumbs-up reaction had been hanging its own thread forever, silently, since the feature first shipped (PR #334) — this is very likely why the whole feature "never worked."
  
  Diagnosis methodology: direct SSH + journalctl log inspection on the live host (not guesswork), a controlled live reproduction (deliberately reverting the deadlock fix to confirm the new regression test actually catches it, then restoring), and repeated live end-to-end tests with Gary reacting in real time while watching server logs, culminating in a clean multi-cycle test (react -> dispatch -> real completed turn with voice reply, repeated 4x without a single hang).
  
  ~120 minutes across the full arc: initial bug report -> live SSH/journalctl diagnosis -> 7 PRs authored, tested (98+ automated tests updated/added, including a regression test proven to catch the exact deadlock via before/after verification) -> merged -> 3 separate multi-service deploys (each verified via systemctl ActiveEnterTimestamp across all 4 services, not just git log) -> final live confirmation.
